en.headline: Court of Appeal dismisses senior officer’s challenge to fraud conviction
en.dek: Superintendent Harbour Chan Hoi-kong’s appeal against his 6½-year sentence for securing more than HK$26 million in mortgages by concealing his police rank is rejected in full.
body: The Court of Appeal on Monday dismissed the appeals of Superintendent Harbour Chan Hoi-kong and a businessman against their convictions and sentences for mortgage fraud. Chan had been sentenced to six and a half years’ imprisonment after being found guilty of two counts of fraud relating to loans totalling more than HK$26 million.

In a written judgment, the court upheld the finding that Chan knowingly made false claims in mortgage applications submitted in 2019, stating he was the general manager of a food trading company rather than a serving police officer. The co-accused, former chief inspector Wong Ho-ngai, also lost his appeal against a five-year term.

Chan, who had previously commented publicly on social media under the name Harbour Sir, remains in custody. The judgment confirms the original trial court’s conclusions on both liability and sentence.

zh.headline: 警司陳凱港按揭欺詐上訴全遭駁回
zh.dek: 上訴庭駁回「海港Sir」陳凱港及同案商人就定罪及判刑的全部上訴，維持6年半監禁。
body: 上訴庭周一頒下書面判詞，駁回警司陳凱港（人稱「海港Sir」）及商人汪浩毅就按揭欺詐案定罪及判刑的全部上訴。陳凱港早前被裁定兩項欺詐罪成，判監6年半；汪浩毅則被判監5年。
法官維持原審裁斷，指陳凱港在2019年申請超過2,600萬元按揭貸款時，明知而虛報自己任職私人公司總經理，隱瞞其警司身份。同案被告汪浩毅的上訴同樣被駁回。
陳凱港早前曾在社交媒體以「海港Sir」名義活躍發言。他現時繼續服刑，判詞確認原審對罪責及刑期的結論。
